item.title: Daniel (Full Book 1-12)
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Daniel — Wheel of Heaven Translation. Full book (chs 1-12). The foundational Hebrew Bible apocalypse + the principal Second Temple Jewish apocalyptic text. 12 chapters / 357 verses covering the six court tales (chs 1-6) and the six apocalyptic visions (chs 7-12).

Bilingual structure — the only Hebrew Bible book with intra-book language transitions: Hebrew Dan 1:1-2:4a + 8:1-12:13 + Aramaic Dan 2:4b-7:28. The transition occurs within verse 2:4 (marked by the Hebrew ʾărāmît "in Aramaic"); Dan 8:1 returns to Hebrew without explicit marker. DSS 4Q112 (the OLDEST Daniel witness, late 2nd c. BCE per Ulrich et al. DJD XVI 2000) confirms the bilingual structure was original, not a late editorial decision. This is the project's first bilingual single-book translation.

Per-verse layered witness reconstruction: Masoretic Text (Hebrew + Aramaic per BHS Codex Leningradensis B19A 1008 CE) as PRIMARY; Dead Sea Scrolls Daniel fragments (4Q112 Daniela late 2nd c. BCE; 4Q113 Danielb late 1st c. BCE - early 1st c. CE; 4Q114 Danielc mid-1st c. CE; 4Q115 Daniele late 1st c. BCE; 4Q116 Danielf late 2nd c. BCE; 1Q71-1Q72; 6Q7 papyrus) as SECONDARY where divergent or text-critically significant; Old Greek + Theodotion-Greek (Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2) as TERTIARY where significant.

Sources: Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia (BHS, Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich, E., et al., 'Daniel' in Qumran Cave 4 XI: Psalms to Chronicles (DJD XVI, Oxford 2000); Collins, J. J., Daniel (Hermeneia, Minneapolis 1993) — THE standard modern critical commentary; Goldingay, J. E., Daniel (WBC 30, Dallas 1989); Hartman, L. F., and Di Lella, A. A., The Book of Daniel (Anchor Bible 23, Garden City 1978); Newsom, C. A., and Breed, B. W., Daniel (OTL, Louisville 2014); Montgomery, J. A., Daniel (ICC, Edinburgh 1927; PD baseline); Charles, R. H., Daniel (Oxford 1929; PD); ASV 1901 (PD English baseline); Ziegler, J., and Munnich, O., Susanna, Daniel, Bel et Draco (Septuaginta XVI.2, Göttingen 1999); Casey, M., Son of Man (1979); Bauckham, R., The Climax of Prophecy (1993) + Jesus and the God of Israel (2008); Hurtado, L. W., One God, One Lord (1988); Boyarin, D., The Jewish Gospels (2012); Beale, G. K., The Book of Revelation (NIGTC 1999); Aune, D. E., Revelation (WBC 52, 1997); Nickelsburg, G. W. E., Resurrection, Immortality, and Eternal Life (2006); Levenson, J. D., Resurrection and the Restoration of Israel (2006); Bickerman, E., Der Gott der Makkabäer (1937); Halperin, D. J., The Faces of the Chariot (1988); Schäfer, P., The Origins of Jewish Mysticism (2009); Hannah, D. D., Michael and Christ (1999); Wolters, A., 'The Riddle of the Scales in Daniel 5' HUCA 62 (1991) + 'Belshazzar's Feast and the Cult of the Moon God Sîn' BBR 5 (1995).

Narrative arc

Chs 1-6: The court tales. The exile to Babylon (ch 1); the four-metals statue dream + the stone cut without hands (ch 2); the fiery furnace + the fourth man "like a son of the gods" (ch 3); Nebuchadnezzar's madness + restoration (ch 4); Belshazzar's feast + MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN (ch 5); the lions' den (ch 6).

Ch 7: The night vision — the load-bearing center of the book + of the entire Second Temple Jewish + early Christian throne-vision tradition. The four beasts + the Ancient of Days (Aramaic ʿAttiq Yomin) seated on a throne of fire + the river of fire + thousand thousands attending + ten thousand times ten thousand standing + books opened + one like a son of man (Aramaic kə-bar enash) coming with clouds of heaven + given dominion + an eternal kingdom.

Chs 8-12: The Hebrew apocalyptic visions. The ram + male goat vision (ch 8); the 70 weeks oracle (ch 9); the angelic-warfare preamble with the seven-attribute angelic figure (ch 10); the Maccabean apocalypse (ch 11); the resurrection + the sealed book + the time, times, and half a time (ch 12).

The Daniel 7 throne-vision

Daniel 7:9-14 is the load-bearing center of the Second Temple Jewish

  • early Christian throne-vision tradition. The vision sets up: (i) THRONES (Aramaic kursawatâ, plural); (ii) the ANCIENT OF DAYS (ʿAttiq Yomin) seated on a throne of fire, white-haired as wool; (iii) the RIVER OF FIRE issuing from before him; (iv) THOUSAND THOUSANDS + TEN THOUSAND TIMES TEN THOUSAND attending; (v) BOOKS OPENED for judgment; (vi) ONE LIKE A SON OF MAN approaching with the clouds of heaven; (vii) ETERNAL DOMINION given.

This translation completes the four-tradition throne-vision wire on the translation surface — Ezekiel 1 ↔ Daniel 7 ↔ 1 Enoch 14 ↔ Shi'ur Qomah ↔ Revelation 1+4 . Daniel 7 was the only piece of this 4-tradition wire previously cited only in glossary apparatus; with Daniel translated, all five traditions are now bidirectionally connected on the translation surface for the first time.

The white-hair-as-wool iconography of Daniel 7:9 is transferred to the risen Christ at Revelation 1:14 — one of the most direct verbal-borrowings in the New Testament from the Aramaic Hebrew Bible.

Cross-corpus density

Six major bidirectional wires established this ship:

  1. Four-tradition throne-vision wire COMPLETED on translation surface — Ezek 1 + Dan 7 + 1 En 14 + Shi'ur Qomah + Rev 1+4.
  2. 70-weeks-of-years × Jubilees jubilee-chronology mathematical lock — Dan 9:24's 490 years = 10 jubilees (10 × 49). Daniel's eschatological-chronological framework is the counterpart of the Jubilees 6:32-38 calendrical-rhythm .
  3. Son of Man trans-traditional cluster — Dan 7:13 → 1 Enoch Similitudes 46-48 + 71 → 4 Ezra 13 → Mark 14:62 + Matthew 26:64 → Revelation 1:7/1:13/14:14 + Acts 7:55-56 . The single most-load-bearing NT Christological text.
  4. Abomination-of-desolation NT-quotation chain — Dan 9:27 + 11:31 + 12:11 → 1 Macc 1:54 → Mt 24:15 + Mk 13:14 → 2 Thess 2:3-4 → Rev 13:14-15.
  5. Resurrection foundational HB text — Dan 12:2 is THE foundational explicit-resurrection text in the Hebrew Bible. Cross-corpus to Isa 26:19 + 2 Macc 7 + Wis 3 + 1 En 22 + 2 Bar 30 + 4 Ezra 7 + Mk 12:25 + Jn 5:28-29 + 1 Cor 15 + 1 Thess 4:16 + Rev 20.
  6. Stone-Christology wire — Dan 2:34-35 → Ps 118:22 + Isa 8:14 + Isa 28:16 → Mk 12:10 + 1 Pet 2:6-8 + 1 Cor 10:4 + Sura 21:96-97.

Additional wires reinforced:

  • Angelic-figure-iconography Rev 1:13-15 verbatim transfer (Dan 10:5-6 seven-attribute description)
  • Michael as Israel's prince-angel cluster (Dan 10:13 first explicit named-Michael in HB)
  • MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN Western art-and-literature reception (Rembrandt 1635 + Handel 1745 + Heine 1827)
  • Sealed-book Daniel-sealed / Rev 22:10 unsealed reception
  • Dan 7:25 + Dan 12:7 time-times-half-a-time formula → Rev 11:2-3 + 12:6 + 12:14 + 13:5

The Maccabean dating

Daniel 11:40-45 contains the foundational scholarly argument for the 167-164 BCE composition window per Collins 1993. The chapter accurately describes the Antiochene persecution up through 11:39 (vaticinium ex eventu), then fails to predict the actual end — the text predicts Antiochus IV's death in Egypt, but Antiochus actually died in Persia in 164 BCE during a campaign against the Parthians. This genuine-prophecy-failure dates the final form to between the events of 11:39 (167 BCE) and the falsification of 11:40 (164 BCE). The Wheel of Heaven translation preserves the failed prediction without harmonization.

Translation choices preserved

  • Bilingual structure preserved transparently via per-verse text_lang ('he' or 'arc')
  • MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN preserved as Aramaic transliteration on surface (uppercase, four words); MT-duplicated reading (not OG single)
  • Ancient of Days preserved as theophanic title (do not domesticate to "Eternal One")
  • 'one like a son of man' lowercase + indefinite at Dan 7:13 (do NOT pre-resolve to NT Christological "Son of Man")
  • 'anointed one' lowercase at Dan 9:25-26 (do NOT pre-resolve to "Messiah" / "Christ")
  • MT atnach punctuation at Dan 9:25 preserved — distinguishing the 7-weeks + 62-weeks structure (vs the KJV/NIV '7 + 62 = 69' collapse)
  • 'abomination of desolation' preserved as NT-quotation form (Mt 24:15 + Mk 13:14)
  • 'seventy weeks' without expansion to "weeks of years" on surface (metaphorical-weeks-as-years sense preserved in apparatus)
  • Michael preserved as proper noun; 'prince' preserved over Greek-translation 'archangel' (which derives from later tradition)
  • BHS verse-numbering preserved (notably 6:1 = English 5:31)
  • rabbîm "many" ambiguity preserved at Dan 12:2 (not resolved to "all" or "some")
  • 'time, times, and half a time' preserved as established English idiom (do NOT translate to "3.5 years")
  • 1290 days + 1335 days preserved literally at Dan 12:11-12 (no harmonization, no day-year conversion)
  • The unfulfilled prediction at 11:40-45 preserved without harmonization — the foundational scholarly evidence for the 167-164 BCE Maccabean dating per Collins 1993
  • NO archaic forms; NO Sitchin/WoH/ancient-astronaut framing on surface
  • NO Christian-typological pre-resolution of Dan 2:34-35 stone + 3:25 fourth-man + 7:13 Son of Man + 9:25-26 anointed-one + 10:4-6 angelic-figure + 11:36-39 + 12:1 antagonist + 12:2 resurrection
  • All Christological + Sitchin + Raëlian-canon reception preserved at glossary-apparatus level only (acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework)

The translation was drafted by Claude Opus 4.7 and edited through the Wheel of Heaven Translation Program pipeline (Translator → Editor → Reviewer). 12 new central glossary entries (all claim_type=direct)

  • 10 existing-entry extensions + 10 per-translation overlay entries; central glossary v2.68.0 → v2.69.0; per-translation overlay v1.0.0 → v1.1.0. All 357 verses reviewer-approved; zero lens-leakage flags; zero speculative-claim entries.

The Greek Daniel expansions — Prayer of Azariah + Song of the Three Young Men (inserted at 3:23-24 in OG + Theodotion), Susanna (Greek ch 13), Bel and the Dragon (Greek ch 14) — are OUTSIDE this Ship A scope. The Ship A translation covers only the MT Hebrew + Aramaic chs 1-12.

The methodology is documented at Source-Text Translation.

  • Jubilees (Ship A: Primeval + Patriarchal Frame) — the Hebrew Enochian companion text; Jub 6 jubilee-chronology bidirectionally locks Dan 9 70-weeks

item.title: Jubilees (Ship A: Primeval + Patriarchal Frame)
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Jubilees Ship A: The Primeval + Patriarchal Frame (chs 1-12) — Wheel of Heaven Translation. The principal Hebrew-language Enochian companion text + the most extensively cross-corpus-engaged non-canonical text in Second Temple Jewish literature. 12 chapters / 373 verses, from Moses on Sinai through Abraham's iconoclasm at Ur.

Per-verse layered witness reconstruction: Hebrew Dead Sea Scrolls fragments (4Q216 dated late 2nd c. BCE per Milik-VanderKam DJD XIII 1994, with additional witnesses 4Q218 + 11Q12 across Ship A scope) as PRIMARY where preserved; Greek patristic citations (Epiphanius De mensuris et ponderibus 21-24 per Dean 1935) SECONDARY where extant — notably the table-of-nations + sub-allotments material at chs 8-9; Ge'ez (Ethiopic) — the only complete witness — TERTIARY and fallback (VanderKam 1989 CSCO 510-511 + Charles 1902 PD).

Hebrew is the original composition language. Greek translation existed but survives only in patristic fragments. Hebrew DSS coverage of Ship A scope is sparse — only chs 1-2 (4Q216 substantial) + ch 2:26-27 (4Q218 Sabbath) + sparse 11Q12 fragments at chs 4 + 5:1 + (probably) ch 8 have Hebrew witnesses; chs 3, 6-12 are Ge'ez-primary with sparse Greek-secondary at chs 8-9.

Sources: Milik, J. T., and VanderKam, J. C., 'Jubilees' in Qumran Cave 4: VIII, Parabiblical Texts, Part 1 (DJD XIII, Oxford 1994) — THE foundational publication of the DSS Hebrew Jubilees fragments; VanderKam, J. C., The Book of Jubilees: A Critical Text and Translation (CSCO 510-511; Scriptores Aethiopici 87-88; Leuven 1989) — THE standard modern critical Ge'ez edition + English; Charles, R. H., The Book of Jubilees, or the Little Genesis (London 1902; PD); VanderKam, J. C., Jubilees: A Commentary in Two Volumes (Hermeneia, Minneapolis 2018) — THE standard modern critical commentary; Segal, M., The Book of Jubilees: Rewritten Bible, Redaction, Ideology and Theology (JSJSup 117, Leiden 2007); Kugel, J. L., A Walk through Jubilees (JSJSup 156, Leiden 2012); Werman, C., Sefer ha-Yovelim (Jerusalem 2015); van Ruiten, J. T. A. G. M., Primaeval History Interpreted: The Rewriting of Genesis 1-11 in the Book of Jubilees (JSJSup 66, 2000); Scott, J. M., Geography in Early Judaism and Christianity: The Book of Jubilees (SNTS Monograph 113, 2002).

Narrative arc

Ch 1 — Moses ascends Sinai for 40 days + 40 nights; God predicts Israel's apostasy + restoration; the heavenly tablets are dictated to Moses through the angel of the presence (malak ha-panim) — the chief celestial mediator + the dictator of the entire book.

Ch 2 — The angel of the presence recites the seven-days-of-creation in the Genesis 1 pattern, with embedded Jubilees-distinctive angelology (the seven categories of angels created on Day 1) and proto-calendrical detail (the luminaries-for-signs formula at 2:9). The Sabbath ordinance is established with the angel of the presence keeping Sabbath in heaven alongside Israel.

Ch 3 — Eden + the woman from the rib + Adam's naming of animals

  • the fall + the Jubilees-distinctive detail that the serpent's punishment includes loss of speech ('their mouth was sealed... that they no longer spoke'). The 80-day + 40-day post-birth purification time-doublings are the foundational text for Lev 12. Adam burns incense as proto-priestly Adam.

Ch 4 — Adam's descendants through Cain + Awan + Azura to Noah. Jub 4:5 establishes the measure-for-measure principle ('by the stone... his house fell upon him and he died'). Jub 4:17-26 is THE foundational Enoch-as-celestial-scribe text — Enoch is the FIRST of humanity to learn writing, composes a calendrical compendium, receives apocalyptic-historical revelation, spends 6 jubilees of years with the angels, writes the indictment of the Watchers, is taken into Eden, and serves as celestial-priest + judge. Jub 4:30 — the 1000-year-day midrash on Gen 5:5 (cross-corpus to Ps 90:4 + 2 Pet 3:8).

Ch 5 — The compressed Watchers narrative parallel to 1 Enoch 6-11 (Hebrew-primary at 5:1 via 11Q12). Jubilees uses malake el 'angels of God' rather than the Genesis 6:1 bnei elohim 'sons of God' — a deliberate disambiguation. The giants slaughter each other prior to the Flood (5:7-9). Jub 5:13 — the heavenly tablets contain all judgments in righteousness. Jub 5:17-19 — the foundational Yom Kippur etiology.

Ch 6 — The Noachic covenant + the seven Noahide commands (blood-prohibition + violence-prohibition; cross-corpus to b. Sanhedrin 56a-60a + Acts 15). Jub 6:17-22 is Jubilees' foundational establishment of Shavuot as the covenant-renewal feast. Jub 6:32-38 is THE FOUNDATIONAL 364-day-solar-calendar polemic: "observe the years according to this reckoning — 364 days, and they will constitute a complete year" (6:32). The sharpest polemic verse — 6:36 "they will make the moon disturb the seasons" — is the defining polemical statement of the calendrical-identity-dispute that separated the Qumran-Enochic-Jubilees community from the proto-Rabbinic luni-solar tradition.

Ch 7 — Noah's vineyard + drunkenness + curse of Ham/Canaan; Noah's testament to his grandsons; the tripartite-giants nomenclature (Naphidim + Nephilim + Elyo at 7:22); proto-Mastema material at 7:27.

Chs 8-9 — The table-of-nations + land-division-by-lot under angelic supervision. Greek-primary at 8:12, 8:22, 8:25 (Epiphanius Greek). Jub 8:19 is THE EXPLICIT three-holy-mountains formula: Mount Zion as the navel-of-the-earth + Mount Sinai as the center-of-the-desert + Mount of the East / Eden-mountain as the center-of-the-world — extending the existing 7-tradition cosmic-mountain cluster to an 8-tradition cluster. The 9:14-15 oath of binding establishes the cosmographic-justification of the conquest-etiology.

Ch 10 — Mastema introduced at 10:7-9 — the prince-of-the-spirits petitions God to leave 1/10 of the demons unbound. One of the earliest extant proper-noun designations of the Satan-figure in Second Temple Judaism. Noah's medicinal book at 10:10-14 — the foundational text for the Sefer Refuot tradition (cross-corpus to b. Pesachim 56a where Hezekiah hides the Book of Cures). The Tower of Babel with Jubilees-distinctive wind-overthrow detail (10:21 — "the Lord sent a great wind against the tower and overthrew it onto the ground") + seventy-languages dispersal (10:26).

Ch 11 — Abram's birth + Mastema directs idolatry (11:3) + sends ravens against Abram's seed (11:11; Abram drives them away by speaking — foundational for the Abram-as-child-iconoclast tradition).

Ch 12 — Abraham's iconoclasm. Jub 12:12-14 is THE EARLIEST EXTANT TEXT of the Abraham-iconoclasm-fire tradition: Abram burns down 'the house of idols' (12:12) + Haran dies trying to rescue the idols (12:14). This is the seed of the trans-Abrahamic tradition spanning Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8 + Genesis Rabbah 38:13 + b. Bava Batra 91a (the rabbinic Ur-Kasdim as 'fire of the Chaldees' midrash)

  • Qur'an Sura 21:51-71 + 37:83-98 + 6:74-79 + 19:41-50 (Ibrahim cast into the furnace). Jub 12:19 — Abram's anti-Mastema prayer to El Elyon. Jub 12:25-26 is THE EARLIEST EXTANT TEXT of the Hebrew-as- creation-language tradition — the angel opens Abram's mouth + ears and teaches him Hebrew, "the language that had been from the beginning of the world but had been forgotten" at Babel; Abram then reads the pre-Mosaic Enochic + Noachic library.

Cross-corpus density

Jubilees is the principal native-Hebrew witness to: the Watchers tradition (parallel to 1 En 6-11); Enoch-as-celestial-scribe (Jub 4:17-26 — the foundational text for the Enoch-Metatron tradition); the heavenly tablets motif (densest extant articulation, 25+ occurrences); the giants-become-evil-spirits demonology (Jub 10:1-6 parallel to 1 En 15:8); the 364-day solar calendar polemic (Jub 6:32-38 foundational; 1 En 72-82 technical implementation).

Ten major bidirectional wires established or extended this pass:

  1. Mastema as the earliest extant Satan-figure designation — bidirectional with CD 16:5 + 1QS 3:18-25 + 1QM 13:11 + Test. Levi 19.
  2. Heavenly tablets densest extant articulation — extends v2.67.0 1 Enoch 81 entry; bidirectional to Dan 7:10 + Rev 5:1 + Rev 20:12.
  3. Enoch-as-scribe foundation — Jub 4:17-26 the earliest systematic articulation; bidirectional to 1 En 12-13 + 3 Enoch / Metatron tradition.
  4. 364-day calendar polemic foundation — Jub 6:32-38 + Jub 6:36 foundational polemic; CD 16:2-3 identifies Jubilees as calendrical authority.
  5. Abraham-iconoclasm-fire trans-Abrahamic tradition — Jub 12:12-14 the earliest extant text; bidirectional to Apoc. Abraham + Genesis Rabbah 38:13 + b. Bava Batra 91a + Qur'an Sura 21/37/6/19.
  6. Three-holy-mountains omphalos extension — Jub 8:19 (Zion + Sinai + Mt-of-the-East) extends the cosmic-mountain cluster.
  7. Giants-become-evil-spirits demonology — Jub 10:1-6 + 1 En 15:8-12 bidirectional.
  8. Hebrew-as-creation-language tradition — Jub 12:25-26 the earliest text; bidirectional to b. Sanhedrin 38b + Genesis Rabbah 18:4 + Jerome + Augustine.
  9. Tower-of-Babel wind-overthrow tradition — Jub 10:21 the earliest specific wind-overthrow; bidirectional to Pseudo-Philo + Sib. Or.
    • 3 Bar + b. Sanhedrin 109a.
  10. Sefer Refuot / Noah's medicinal book — Jub 10:10-14 the foundational text; bidirectional to b. Pesachim 56a + Aramaic Levi 51-57 + Mesopotamian apkallū knowledge-transmission framework.

Jubilees in the canon

Jubilees was widely read at Qumran — the 15+ DSS witnesses make it one of the most-attested non-canonical texts in the Scrolls — and explicitly cited at CD 16:2-3 (the Damascus Document) as authoritative on calendrical questions. It is canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (where it appears as Kufale 'division') and in the Beta Israel (Ethiopian Jewish) tradition. It survived in these canon-traditions but was lost to the wider Christian + rabbinic traditions until the modern recovery.

Translation choices preserved

  • Per-verse layered witness attribution — Hebrew DSS primary where preserved; Greek Epiphanius secondary at chs 8-9; Ge'ez tertiary + fallback
  • Mastema preserved as proper noun (not "Satan" / "the Adversary" on surface) — the Jubilees-specific identity is philologically distinct from later cosmic-dualist Satan-figure
  • Heavenly tablets (luhot ha-shamayim) preserved as a fixed technical phrase across all 25+ occurrences
  • Angel of the presence (malak ha-panim) preserved as a fixed Jubilees-distinctive title
  • Three holy mountains trio preserved as proper nouns (Mount Zion
    • Mount Sinai + Mount of the East / Eden-mountain)
  • Watchers / malake el / bnei elohim — "Watchers" / "angels of God" / "sons of God" per established 1 Enoch precedent
  • 364-day-calendar polemical voice preserved without softening or pre-resolution
  • Mt-of-the-East identification ambiguity preserved at 8:19 (three competing scholarly identifications noted in commentary)
  • Mastema vs Beliar variant at 1:20: principal Ge'ez Bēlhārā reading "Beliar" preserved
  • 1/10 demon-bargain at 10:8-9: bargain-narrative voice preserved without harmonization with later cosmic-dualism
  • NO archaic forms; NO Sitchin/WoH/ancient-astronaut framing on surface
  • Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework at the Mastema-as-rival- Elohim-faction reading + the Watchers-as-Elohim-civilization reading lives in commentary apparatus only

The translation was drafted by Claude Opus 4.7 and edited through the Wheel of Heaven Translation Program pipeline (Translator → Editor → Reviewer). 12 new central glossary entries (all claim_type=direct)

  • 10 existing-entry extensions + 7 per-translation overlay entries; central glossary v2.67.0 → v2.68.0; per-translation overlay v1.0.0 → v1.1.0. All 373 verses reviewer-approved; zero lens-leakage flags; zero speculative-claim entries.

Ship B (Jubilees 13-50) remains a future ship — the patriarchal narrative from Abraham's call through the Sinai-revelation. Includes: the binding of Isaac through Mastema (Jub 17-18); Jacob's Bethel theophany (Jub 27); the Levi-priesthood etiology (Jub 30-32); Joseph (Jub 39-46); Moses + the Exodus + Sinai (Jub 47-50). Estimated scope: ~38 chapters, ~900+ verses — significantly larger than Ship A.

The methodology is documented at Source-Text Translation.

item.title: 1 Enoch (Watchers + Astronomical Book)
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
1 Enoch — Wheel of Heaven Translation. Ships A+B: the Book of the Watchers (chs 1-36) + the Astronomical Book (chs 72-82). The most directly WoH-engaged text in the entire pseudepigrapha — named in Yes... I am Raelian among the texts "closer to the truth," alongside the Mahābhārata, Kojiki, Popol Vuh, and the Epic of Gilgamesh.

47 chapters / 403 verses across two compositions, produced from a per-verse layered witness reconstruction:

  • Ship A — Book of the Watchers (chs 1-36; 248 verses). Aramaic Dead Sea Scrolls fragments (4Q201 / 4Q202 / 4Q204 / 4Q205 / 4Q206 / 4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. BCE) as PRIMARY witness where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus codex (6th c. CE; chs 1-32 substantially complete) SECONDARY; Ge'ez (Ethiopic) — the only complete witness — TERTIARY and fallback. The Greek Akhmim breaks off mid-chapter 32; chs 33-36 are witnessed by Ge'ez alone.
  • Ship B — Astronomical Book / Sefer ha-Mazzalot / Book of the Luminaries (chs 72-82; 155 verses). Aramaic DSS fragments 4Q208 / 4Q209 / 4Q210 / 4Q211 as PRIMARY witness where preserved — 4Q208 is the OLDEST surviving Enoch material overall, dated by Milik 1976 to "the end of the third or beginning of the second century BCE," predating even the Watchers fragments. No Greek witness for chs 72-82 (Akhmim covers only chs 1-32); the layered schema collapses to Aramaic + Ge'ez. Significantly: the Aramaic recension is materially longer than the Ge'ez, with much astronomical detail (lunar synodic tables, gate-by-gate sun tracking, precise day-counts) abbreviated or omitted in the Ethiopic transmission tradition (Milik 1976; Nickelsburg–VanderKam 2012; Drawnel 2011).

Sources: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (the foundational publication of the Qumran Aramaic fragments); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (Greek + commentary); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 (Hermeneia, chs 1-36, 81-108); Nickelsburg–VanderKam 2012 1 Enoch 2 (Hermeneia, chs 37-82) — THE standard modern critical commentary on the Astronomical Book; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (PD, Ge'ez baseline); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Ge'ez scholarly standard); Neugebauer 1985 The 'Astronomical' Chapters of the Ethiopic Book of Enoch (72-82) — the specialist scientific commentary; Tigchelaar–García Martínez DJD XXXVI (2000); VanderKam 1998 Calendars in the Dead Sea Scrolls; Beckwith 1996; Glessmer 1999; Drawnel 2011 The Aramaic Astronomical Book; Stern 2001; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels and the History of Judaism and Christianity; Stuckenbruck 2007.

Ship A — Book of the Watchers (chs 1-36)

Enoch's opening theophany prophecy (chs 1-5; the Jude 14-15 quote site at 1:9); the Watchers' descent on Mount Hermon (ch 6) + the 200 sons-of-heaven taking human wives + the 20 Watcher chiefs (Šemiḥazah, ʿAzazʾēl, Bărāqʾēl, Kōkabʾēl, etc.); the engendering of the Nephilim giants (ch 7); Asael's knowledge-transmission catalog — metallurgy, weapons-craft, cosmetics, magic, astronomical-divination (ch 8); the archangels' intercession (ch 9); the Most High's commission + Asael bound at Dudael (ch 10); Enoch the scribe-intercessor (chs 12-13); the throne-vision and the Great Glory (ch 14 — the four-tradition throne-vision cluster); the indictment-sealed + the giants-become-evil-spirits demonology (chs 15-16); Enoch's cosmic tours through the abyss + mountains-of- fire + the seven mountains of God (chs 17-19, 24-25); the list of seven archangels (ch 20; Aramaic 4 vs Greek 7 textual variant preserved); the prison of the fallen stars (ch 21); the four hollow places of the dead (ch 22 — foundational intermediate-state doctrine); the tree of life on the paradisiacal mountain (chs 24-25); Jerusalem as the center of the earth (ch 26); the Valley of Hinnom = Gehenna (ch 27 — fountainhead text for the 12 NT geenna references); the eastern paradise + aromatic trees (chs 28-31); the tree of wisdom = Genesis 3 tree of knowledge (ch 32 — Sophia/Hokhmah fountainhead); the four-corners gates of heaven (chs 33-36; Ge'ez witness only).

Ship B — Astronomical Book (chs 72-82)

Ch 72 — Uriel's prologue + the sun's annual circuit through the 6 eastern + 6 western gates. The central calendrical statement at 72:32: the sun completes 364 days "and nothing is added to it" — foundational for the Qumran solar-calendar tradition.

Chs 73-74 — the moon's nature; the 354-day lunar year vs the 364-day solar year; the 10-day annual gap; multi-year reconciliation tabulations. 4Q208 (the oldest Enoch fragment) preserves substantially fuller fractional-light tables than Ge'ez records.

Ch 75 — the four "leaders of thousands" governing the four 91-day quarters of the year + the four epact-days. The sharpest polemic verses: "those who do not add them in — humans err".

Ch 76 — the twelve gates of the four winds (3 per cardinal direction); the differentiated effects of each (rains, snow, fog, dew, beneficial vs destructive winds). Aramaic-primary at 76:1-2.

Ch 77 — the four quarters of the earth; "north as the dwelling of the Most High" (77:2; Aramaic-primary, extending the cosmic- mountain cluster to Ps 48:3 yarkəṯē ṣāp̄ôn + Ugaritic Ṣapunu); the seven mountains + seven rivers.

Ch 78 — the names of sun and moon (corrupted in Ge'ez transmission; preserved verbatim per layered-witness convention); the moon's 14-day waxing + 14-day waning; the 49-unit moonlight grid that 4Q208/4Q209 preserves but Ge'ez compresses.

Ch 79 — Uriel's revelation summary.

Ch 80 — the cosmic-disorder oracle. In the last days the heavenly bodies will deviate, the moon will change its laws, rain will fail, stars will transgress their orbits, and humans will mistake stars for gods. THE central NT cross-corpus chapter: Joel 2:30-31 → Mt 24:29 / Mk 13:24-25 / Lk 21:25-26 → Rev 6:12-13 → Sura 81:1-14 + Sura 54:1. The apocryphal-tradition fountainhead bridging Joel and the NT cosmic-signs cluster.

Ch 81 — the heavenly tablets (luḥōt ha-shamayim) that contain all deeds + all generations; Enoch instructed by seven holy ones; the one-year-with-his-children-then-final-assumption commission. Cross-corpus to Jubilees 5/23/30 + Dan 7:10 + Rev 5:1 + Rev 20:12.

Ch 82 — Enoch's instructions to Methuselah; the leaders of the year's four seasons + 12 months + 360 days + 4 epact days. The 364-day Qumran calendar polemic at its sharpest — Aramaic-primary at 82:4-5 from 4Q211. 4Q211 preserves Aramaic continuation BEYOND the Ge'ez ending — confirming Milik's hypothesis that the original Astronomical Book extended significantly further into autumn/winter quarter-leader material that the Ge'ez tradition truncated.

Highest cross-corpus density in the corpus

Seven major bidirectional wires established across Ships A+B:

  1. First 4-tradition throne-vision wire: Ezekiel 1 → Daniel 7 → 1 Enoch 14 → Shi'ur Qomah → Revelation 1 + 4 .
  2. 7-tradition cosmic-mountain cluster (extended from 6): Mt Sinai/Horeb + Mt Ṣapunu + Mt Nimush/Ararat/al-Jūdī + Eden-mountain
    • Mt Hermon + the seven mountains of 1 Enoch 18 + 24-25 + the north-as-dwelling-of-the-Most-High of 1 Enoch 77:2.
  3. Watcher canonical-engagement framework — acknowledgment-without- endorsement at the Watchers-as-Elohim + Asael-as-technology-transfer sites; parallel to the Anunnaki / apkallū framework already in production.
  4. NT × 1 Enoch wire: Jude 14-15 verbatim quote of 1 Enoch 1:9; Jude 6 + 2 Peter 2:4 (Watchers' confinement); Revelation 6:9-10 (four hollow places); Revelation 8:2 (seven archangels); Revelation 22:2 (tree of life); 12 NT geenna references (Valley of Hinnom).
  5. Enoch–Metatron tradition wire: 1 Enoch 12-13 + 81 (scribe + heavenly tablets + final assumption) → 3 Enoch Sefer Hekhalot enthroned-Metatron.
  6. Sophia / Hokhmah tradition fountainhead: 1 Enoch 32 tree of wisdom → Proverbs 8 + Wisdom of Solomon 7-9.
  7. Cosmic-signs cluster: 1 Enoch 80 → Joel 2 → Synoptic Olivet Discourse → Revelation 6 → Sura 81 / Sura 54 — the apocryphal- tradition fountainhead bridge.

The Qumran 364-day-calendar polemic

The Astronomical Book is the principal extant statement of the Qumran community's 364-day solar calendar, sharpest at 72:32 ("nothing is added to it"), 75:2-3 ("humans err — they do not reckon the four epact-days"), and 82:4-6 (the beatitude-polemic in Aramaic from 4Q211). The same calendar reappears in Jubilees 6:32-38 (the parallel polemical text) and is implemented in the 4Q319-4Q330 Mishmarot calendrical texts, CD 16:2-3 (calendar-as-covenant in the Damascus Document), and 4QMMT (the calendar as a mark of identity-separation from mainstream Second Temple Judaism's lunar-solar reckoning). Standard scholarship: VanderKam 1998 Calendars in the Dead Sea Scrolls; Beckwith 1996; Glessmer 1999; Stern 2001.

The Watchers myth (Ship A)

The 200 sons-of-heaven (bnei elohim; Aramaic bn-ilm; Greek huioi tou theou) descend under Šemiḥazah to take human wives (1 En 6-7) and beget the Nephilim — directly expanding Genesis 6:1-4 into a fully-developed mythological narrative. Asael (Aramaic ʿAśāʾēl; Greek + Ge'ez Azazel) teaches humanity metallurgy, swords, knives, shields, breastplates, mining, jewelry, cosmetics, alchemy, and astrology (1 En 8:1-3) — the canon's central Enoch citation site. The Watchers-as-Elohim-civilization reading and the Asael-as-Elohim-technology-transfer reading are preserved as canonical-reception phenomena at the apparatus level only (glossary entries + per-verse commentary); the translation surface preserves the scholarly mainstream reading (Reed 2005 Fallen Angels; Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia; Stuckenbruck 2014). item.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
item.author: Unknown

Gilgamesh Tablet XI (Wheel of Heaven Translation) — the Standard Babylonian recension Flood narrative. The fifth Mesopotamian text in the WoH corpus (after Enki and Ninmah, the Sumerian Flood Story, Enki and Ninhursag, and Adapa) and the single most-canon- named Mesopotamian text — the Raëlian canon (per Yes... 308 lines of Standard Babylonian Akkadian per the George 2003 critical edition line-numbering. Sin-leqi-unninni recension (~1200 BCE; underlying Atrahasis-tradition extends back to the early-2nd-millennium). Primary manuscript witnesses: the Library of Ashurbanipal Nineveh tablets (7th c. BCE; British Museum K series including K.3375 + K.7752 + K.2252 + Sm. 4302 + others; recovered by Layard 1849). Rediscovered by George Smith in 1872 — his 1873 publication The Chaldean Account of the Deluge demonstrated the Mesopotamian antecedent to the biblical Flood narrative.

Sources: George 2003 The Babylonian Gilgamesh Epic (Oxford, 2 vols) — THE modern critical edition; Thompson 1930 The Epic of Gilgamish (PD critical edition with cuneiform copy + transliteration); Smith 1873 The Chaldean Account of the Deluge (PD discovery publication); Foster 2005 Before the Muses 3rd ed. (scholarly modern English baseline). Verification pending against George 2003 critical edition + original Nineveh codicology.

Narrative arc. Gilgamesh's journey to find Utnapishtim the immortal flood-survivor; Utnapishtim recounts how the gods (Anu, Enlil, Ninurta, Ennugi, Ea) decided to flood the earth; Ea's warning to Utnapishtim through the reed-wall; the boat (tebû/eleppu) construction with seven decks; embarkation of family + craftsmen + "the seed of all living creatures"; the six-day-seven-night flood from the Anunnaki + Adad's thunder; the landing on Mt Nimush; the bird-test (dove → swallow → raven); the disembarkation + sacrifice ("the gods gathered like flies"); Enlil's anger + Ea's defense; the deification + immortality grant to Utnapishtim; Gilgamesh's failure (the seven-loaves test); the loss of the plant-of-rejuvenation to the serpent; the return to Uruk.

Highest cross-corpus density in the Mesopotamian sub-corpus. Direct parallels documented per line:

  • Hebrew Bible Genesis 6-9 (Noah narrative) — boat construction, animal loading, flood-duration, bird-test, mountain-landing, sacrifice, divine-promise. Heidel 1946 The Gilgamesh Epic and Old Testament Parallels is the foundational comparative study.
  • Sumerian Flood Story (Ziusudra recension; already in WoH Translation as flood-story-woh) — older Mesopotamian flood-tradition.
  • Akkadian Atrahasis (Lambert-Millard 1969) — Sin-leqi-unninni signals at L189 that Utnapishtim and Atra-ḫasīs are the same character under alternative standing-epithets ("Surpassingly Wise" vs "I-found-life").
  • Berossus Babyloniaca (Hellenistic-period Greek retelling preserved in Eusebius via Polyhistor).
  • Qur'an Surah 11:25-49 (Noah narrative; cf. Mt Nimush ↔ al-Jūdī Q 11:44).

  • v2.61.0 har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim (Hebrew Bible Exodus)

Mark 16 (Wheel of Heaven Translation) — the Resurrection narrative + the longer-ending textual-critical site. The Raëlian canon engages Mark 16:18 (snake-handling passage) and Mark 16:19 (Ascension) in Extraterrestrials Took Me To Their Planet — acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applied per the established Shi'ur Qomah / Qur'an / Exodus / Matthew precedents.

The longer-ending textual-critical dispute. Mark 16 ends at verse 8 (ephobounto gar "for they were afraid") in Codex Vaticanus (B/03) and Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) — the two earliest substantial uncial witnesses. The "longer ending" Mark 16:9-20 (containing the resurrection appearances + the Ascension at v19 + the snake-handling and poison-immunity passage at v18) is ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Codex Bobiensis (k, Old Latin) + Sinaitic Syriac. The longer ending is PRESENT in Codex Alexandrinus + Codex Bezae + later Byzantine tradition. Consensus modern critical view (Metzger UBS Textual Commentary; Aland-Aland; Marcus 2009 AB; Collins 2007 Hermeneia): the longer ending is a 2nd-century scribal addition to harmonize Mark with the other Gospels.

This translation preserves the canonical longer-ending text on the surface (verses 9-20 rendered as canonical Mark 16) — same pattern as Matthew's Conybeare-hypothesis handling at Mt 28:19 — with the textual-criticism dispute documented at the central glossary entry mark-16-9-20-longer-ending-textual-critical-site (v2.64.0).

20 verses sourced from Vaticanus + Sinaiticus (primary 4th-c. uncial witnesses) + P45 Chester Beatty I (~250 CE, contains substantial Mark) cross-collation + NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus. Scholarly references: Metzger 1994, France 2002 NIGTC, Marcus 2000/2009 AB, Collins 2007 Hermeneia. Verification pending against the original codicology.

item.title: The Gospel According to Matthew
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Matthew (Wheel of Heaven Translation) — the most heavily cited New Testament book in the Raëlian canon. The Role of Christ engages Matthew across 17 of its 28 chapters; this translation covers the eight highest-citation-density chapters as the canon-closure selection. The project's first Christian-tradition text and first Koine Greek source text.

The 8 canon-cited chapters:

  • Mt 1 — the genealogy of Jesus + the virgin-birth narrative
  • Mt 5 — Sermon on the Mount Pt I (Beatitudes; salt and light; "not to abolish but to fulfill"; the antitheses)
  • Mt 6 — Sermon on the Mount Pt II (alms; the Lord's Prayer; fasting; treasure in heaven; anxiety)
  • Mt 7 — Sermon on the Mount Pt III (judgment; ask-seek-knock; the Golden Rule; the narrow gate; the two builders)
  • Mt 13 — THE EXPLICIT CANON SITE: the kingdom parables (Sower, Tares, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Hidden Treasure, Pearl, Net). Raël's The Role of Christ reads the Parable of the Sower as "the description of life being seeded on multiple worlds" — the four soil-types interpreted literally as four planet-types receiving the Elohim seeding-of-life.
  • Mt 17 — the Transfiguration + the demoniac boy + the temple-tax
  • Mt 25 — Ten Virgins + Talents + Sheep and Goats (the final judgment)
  • Mt 28 — the Resurrection + the Great Commission

287 verses across 8 chapters. The early-manuscript approach parallels the Qur'an translation's Tübingen + Codex Parisino-petropolitanus method: source the text from the earliest substantially-complete codices and cross-collate against the earlier papyri where they preserve target verses.

Sources:

  • Codex Vaticanus (B / 03) — Vatican Library Gr. 1209, ~325-350 CE — primary 4th-c. uncial witness; contains complete Matthew; the standard NA28/UBS5 critical-text base
  • Codex Sinaiticus (א / 01) — British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai
    • Leipzig + St. Petersburg, ~330-360 CE — only complete uncial codex; secondary primary witness
  • Cross-collation against early papyri where target verses are preserved:
    • P104 (Oxford P.Oxy 4404; ~150 CE) — among the EARLIEST surviving Matthew witnesses, ~150-200 years before the great uncials
    • P64+P67 (Magdalen + Barcelona; late 2nd c. CE) — Mt 5:20-22, 25-28 + Mt 26
    • P77 (~200 CE) — Mt 23:30-39
    • P103 (P.Oxy 4403; late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE) — Mt 13:55-57, 14:3-5 (cross-collation for our Mt 13)
    • P45 (Chester Beatty I; ~250 CE) — substantial Matthew portions including Mt 20-26 (cross-collation for our Mt 25)

Critical apparatus reference: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th edition, 2012), UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014), SBLGNT (Society of Biblical Literature, Holmes 2010), THGNT (Tyndale House, Jongkind 2017).

Three highest-citation-density Raëlian-canon lens-risk sites — all managed with explicit named verbatim disavowals:

  • Mt 13:3-23 (the Parable of the Sower) — THE single most-load-bearing canon-engagement in the entire Matthew translation. Three reading-strata preserved: mainstream Christian-tradition (Davies-Allison ICC, Luz Hermeneia, France NICNT, Snodgrass 2008); Jewish-historical-critical (Levine 2014 Short Stories by Jesus); Raëlian-canon panspermia. Verbatim acknowledgment-without-endorsement per the Shi'ur Qomah parasangs
    • Qur'an inshiqāq al-qamar + Exodus pillar/parting/manna/theophany precedents.
  • Mt 17:1-9 (the Transfiguration) — Raëlian-canon "Elohim manifest in glory + Moses+Elijah appearing" acknowledgment-without- endorsement. The bath-qol voice at Mt 17:5 is a four-layered scriptural allusion: Ps 2:7 (ben-Yhwh) + Isa 42:1 (servant-chosen)
    • Deut 18:15 (prophet-like-Moses) + Mt 3:17 (the baptism-voice). Allison 1993 The New Moses.
  • Mt 28:18-20 (the Great Commission) — Raëlian-canon engagement + the Conybeare 1901 hypothesis preserved without adjudication (Eusebius's pre-Nicene citations of Mt 28:19 use a shorter en tō onomati mou form; Conybeare proposed the trinitarian formula is a later interpolation. All extant Greek MSS preserve the trinitarian formula; the Didache 7 + Justin 1 Apology 61 attest the formula in early-2nd-c. usage). WoH-Translation renders the canonical text on surface; documents Conybeare as one scholarly position.

Plus four other major lens-risk sites:

  • Mt 1:22-23 (the virgin birth + Isa 7:14) — LXX parthenos (virgin) vs Hebrew ʿalmâ (young woman) philological dispute preserved-not-adjudicated. Brown 1993 The Birth of the Messiah
    • Levine 2014 Jewish Annotated New Testament Jewish-scholarly counterpoint.
  • Mt 5:17 ("I came not to abolish but to fulfill") — locus classicus of Jewish-Christian dialogue. Explicit Christian-supersessionist disavowal: this verse does NOT support a reading where the Torah is superseded. The verb plērōsai philological breadth preserved (complete / do / fully realize).
  • Mt 6:9-13 (the Lord's Prayer) — the WoH-Translation renders WITHOUT the Byzantine doxology at 6:13b (consensus modern critical-text — absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + earliest mss; Metzger UBS Textual Commentary). The doxology is documented as a textual variant. The epiousios hapax at 6:11 — three classical readings preserved (daily / for-tomorrow / supersubstantial).
  • Mt 25:40 ("the least of these brothers") — three reading-strata preserved per Gray 1989 The Least of My Brothers: A History of Interpretation: (A) universalist (all suffering humanity); (B) ecclesial-particularist (Christians-in-distress); (C) Jewish-particularist (Jewish-people-in-distress). The v45 absence of tōn adelphōn mou is the key counter-datum.

Translation choices preserved:

  • theos → "God"; kyrios → "Lord"; Iēsous → "Jesus"; Christos → "Christ" (Greek-Hebrew-Aramaic cognate documented at central entries)
  • Genealogical text: preserve four women named (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, "wife of Uriah" Bathsheba) per Brown 1993's four readings
  • makarios in the Beatitudes → "blessed" (KJV/RSV tradition)
  • epiousios in the Lord's Prayer → "daily" (mainstream English tradition); alternatives documented
  • Byzantine doxology at Mt 6:13b → OMITTED (critical-text consensus); documented as variant
  • raca at Mt 5:22 → preserved with parenthetical
  • aiōnios at Mt 25:41, 46 → "eternal" (mainstream); "age-pertaining" documented as scholarly alternative
  • Trinitarian baptismal formula at Mt 28:19 → preserved as canonical text; Conybeare 1901 hypothesis documented at central entry

The new mountain-as-revelation-site-mt (Mt as new-Moses typology — Allison 1993) is bidirectionally wired with the v2.61.0 Exodus har-sinai-horev (Sinai/Horeb as cosmic-mountain) and the v2.57.0 Baal Cycle mount-sapunu-tsafon-cosmic-mountain. item.title: Qur'an — early-manuscript selection
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The Qur'an (Wheel of Heaven Translation, early-manuscript selection) is the project's first Islamic-tradition text and first Arabic-source text. Scope is strictly limited to Suras 21:1–5, 54:1, and 56:15–24 — the only three Qur'anic passages the Raëlian canon engages with chapter-and-verse precision (in Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet). The project engages Islam respectfully and technically; this is not a full-Qur'an translation and does not claim to be.

The early-manuscript approach. Rather than working from the modern Cairo recension (1924 King Fuad edition, based on the late-medieval Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim reading-tradition), this translation works from the rasm — the bare consonantal skeleton, no letter-discrimination dots (iʿjām), no vowel marks (tashkīl) — of the earliest-surviving Qur'anic manuscript-witnesses. The dots and vowel marks were added to Qur'anic manuscripts across the 8th–10th centuries CE; the underlying rasm in the earliest manuscripts is substantially what was copied in the 7th century. Sources:

  • Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 1–5 ← Tübingen Fragment Ma VI 165 (Universitätsbibliothek Tübingen; Hijazi script; radiocarbon-dated 649–675 CE — within 17–43 years of the traditional Uthmanic codification c. 650 CE; contains Suras 17–36). Cross-collated against Codex Parisino-petropolitanus.
  • Sūrat al-Qamar 1 + Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah 15–24 ← Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328 + St. Petersburg / Birmingham / Vatican fragments; Hijazi script; late 7th c.).

Three layers per ayah are preserved in the source files: (1) the rasm (bare consonantal skeleton from the early manuscript); (2) the modern vocalized Arabic (Hafs ʿan ʿĀṣim reading-tradition, Cairo 1924) supplied as the reference vocalization; (3) scientific transliteration (DMG / ALA-LC convention).

The textual-criticism context. The Qur'an's textual transmission is genuinely scholarly-contested in modern manuscript studies. Sadeghi-Goudarzi 2010 frames the early manuscripts as evidence of an early canonical text with limited variation. Hilali 2017 frames the Sanʿāʾ 1 palimpsest evidence as showing "transmission in flux" in the first century AH. Earlier scholarship (Wansbrough 1977, Crone-Cook 1977) proposed later-canonization frameworks that recent manuscript discoveries have substantially nuanced. This translation preserves the textual-criticism dispute rather than adjudicating it.

The Raëlian-canon citation context. Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet cites Sura 21:1–5 (the eschatological-reckoning opening), Sura 54:1 (iqtarabati s-sāʿatu wa-nšaqqa l-qamaru — "the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split"), and Sura 56:15–24 (the paradisal-reception passage). The canon's reading of 54:1 as a literal description of an Elohim-spacecraft propulsion-event that split the moon is its most-explicit "the Qur'an describes ET tech" citation. The WoH-Translation produces the philologically- disciplined version of these passages, not the canon's pre-filtered version, with explicit operational disavowals against Sitchin/Anunnaki/ET-propulsion readings throughout the glossary apparatus. The eight canon-citation paragraphs (21:1, 54:1, 56:17, 56:22 and the surrounding passage) all carry explicit acknowledgment-without-endorsement of the canon's reading — same pattern as the Shi'ur Qomah parasangs precedent.

Five critical lens-risk sites — all managed with verbatim disavowals:

  • 54:1 (inshiqāq al-qamar, "splitting of the moon") — three reading-strata preserved: mainstream Sunni past-miracle (Bukhārī 4864, Muslim 2801, Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr); modernist eschatological- future (al-Manār, Sayyid Quṭb); Raëlian ET-propulsion. Cross-corpus Joel 2:30-31 / Mark 13:24-25 / Acts 2:19-20 / Rev 6:12-13. Verbatim Sitchin / NASA-apologetic / Christian-supersessionist disavowals.
  • 56:22 (ḥūr ʿīn, the "wide-eyed companions") — five reading-strata: classical tafsīr / modern Asad-Pickthall-Arberry / Luxenberg 2000 "white grapes" academically rejected (Stewart 2008, Neuwirth 2003, Saleh 2008) / popular Western "72 virgins" stereotype disavowed (the number 72 is from later weak ḥadīth Tirmidhī 2562, NOT in the Qur'an) / Raëlian disavowed.
  • 56:17 (wildān muḫalladūn, "youths eternal") — Luxenberg "fruits-everlasting" + Raëlian "cloning-immortality" disavowed.
  • 21:1 (iqtaraba li-n-nāsi ḥisābuhum, "the reckoning has drawn near for humanity") — Christian-supersessionist + Raëlian Age-of-Apocalypse disavowals. Cross-corpus Mark 13:32-33 / Matt 24:36-42 / 1 Thess 5:1-3 / 2 Pet 3:3-10 / Joel 2:1-2.
  • The Allah entry — genuine Semitic-cognate documented (Arabic Allāh < al-ilāh; Hebrew Elohim; Aramaic Elāh; Syriac Alāhā — all from shared √ʾ-l-h). Used by Arabic-speaking Christians, Jews, and Muslims. Disavow simplistic-identification (Allah = YHWH; Allah = Trinitarian Father) — the Qur'anic Allah has its own theological profile (strict tawḥīd; rejection of trinitarian and incarnational claims).

The translation is best-effort reconstruction from published facsimiles + the Corpus Coranicum digital apparatus + Sadeghi-Bergmann 2010 + Sadeghi-Goudarzi 2010 + Hilali 2017 + Déroche 2009/2014 + Neuwirth 2014 + Reynolds 2008/2011. Verification against the original manuscript codicology (Tübingen UB; BnF Paris; National Library of Russia St. Petersburg; Cadbury Research Library Birmingham; BAV Vatican) is pending; corrections welcome.

The rasm is preserved in the underlying source files for downstream paleographic and text-critical work; the surface translation engages the rasm-and-Hafs lexical content (consonant across the early Hijazi witnesses and the Cairo Hafs for the target ayahs).

item.title: Shi'ur Qomah
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Shi'ur Qomah (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is the project's first Kabbalah / Jewish-mysticism-tradition text. The text is one of the oldest pieces of Jewish mystical literature (3rd–6th c. CE, with traditions reaching earlier — Scholem 1965 argues for tannaitic-era roots), preserved across Hekhalot literature. It describes the cosmic measurements of the body of the Creator — the divine Yotzer — as a head-to-foot enumeration in which each limb is named with a secret magical name and measured in parasangs (a Persian unit of distance adapted to cosmic scale: one parasang, by the text's own internal logic, is "as much as the entire universe is full"). The framing is a pseudo-tannaitic transmission from R. Yishmael (the famous high priest) through R. Akiva to the Hekhalot mystics. The implicit liturgical-theurgical function: knowing the names and measurements lets the mystic ascend the seven Hekhalot palaces and stand before the throne.

Chapter 1 — Siddur Rabbah recension. Cohen 1985 distinguishes five recensions of Shi'ur Qomah (Sefer Hekhalot, Sefer Razim, Merkavah Rabbah, Siddur Rabbah, Ma'aseh Merkavah); this chapter covers the Siddur Rabbah recension, the most-cited "standard" recension and the one preserved in Sefer Raziel ha-Mal'akh and the medieval Hekhalot anthologies. 67 paragraphs. Includes: the R. Yishmael / Metatron opening transmission (§2); the foundational 236-myriads cosmic-total measurement (§3); the head-to-foot body enumeration with ~40 magical names per limb (§§5–49); R. Akiva's guarantor-formula promising that daily Shi'ur Qomah recitation as Mishnah secures the world-to-come (§41 — the most-cited Shi'ur Qomah passage in rabbinic-liturgical tradition); the Metatron-as-naʿar youth-prince scenes (§52); the cosmic-silence + Ineffable Name theurgical core (§§60–61); and the Ps 8:2 alphabetic-acrostic hymn appendix (§§64–67).

Reception is genuinely contested. Maimonides (Iggeret Teiman; Mishneh Torah, Yesodei ha-Torah 1:8-12; Guide for the Perplexed I:35-36) condemned the text as un-Jewish — calling it "a forgery of a Greek preacher or a Karaite." Conversely, the Hasidei Ashkenaz of medieval Germany (Eleazar of Worms), R. Moses Cordovero (Pardes Rimmonim), the Lurianic Kabbalists, the Hasidic tradition, and modern Hekhalot scholarship (Scholem, Cohen, Schäfer, Halperin, Boustan, Idel) all treat Shi'ur Qomah as serious mystical literature. The WoH translation acknowledges Maimonides' condemnation without adjudicating the dispute — the contested-reception is preserved as part of the text's documented history.

Raëlian-canon engagement. The End of the World and At the Root of All Religions both implicitly cite the Shi'ur Qomah tradition for its parasangs measurements and "height of the creator" passages — making this translation a project priority for closing one of the genuine source-tensions named in the Reference corpus of the Raëlian canon wiki entry. Critical: the WoH-Translation produces the philologically-disciplined version of Shi'ur Qomah, not the canon's pre-filtered version, with explicit operational disavowals against Sitchin/Anunnaki/engineered-deity-body readings throughout the glossary apparatus. The eight Raëlian-canon-flagged paragraphs (§§2, 3, 16, 22, 31, 40, 41, 56) all carry explicit acknowledgment-without-endorsement of the canon's citation.

The translation handles the most distinctive lens-risk landscape in the WoH corpus to date. Extreme anthropomorphism + magical-name theurgical tradition + Maimonidean condemnation + Raëlian-canon citation + cosmic-body-with-measurements (surface similarity to Sitchin-Anunnaki ancient-astronaut readings) + gnostic-syncretism scholarly dispute (Scholem 1965 vs Halperin 1988 / Schäfer 1992 / Boustan 2005) + Christological-typology lens-risk (Boyarin 2012 vs Schäfer 2012 on the Metatron-NT relationship). All sites are managed through named-scholarship attributions, verbatim disavowals where lens-leakage would compromise the source, and preservation of genuinely-contested scholarly disputes where adjudication would force premature closure.

The translation is best-effort reconstruction from Jellinek 1853 Bet ha-Midrasch (PD), Cohen 1985 The Shi'ur Qomah: Texts and Recensions (TSAJ 9 — THE modern critical edition; paywalled), Schäfer 1981 Synopse zur Hekhalot-Literatur (TSAJ 2), and the open- access scholarly portions of all three. Verification against Cohen 1985 is pending; corrections welcome.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel. The interlinear view shows the Hebrew alongside the SBL academic transliteration. Magical names are rendered in ALL-CAPS in the English per a standard scholarly convention (Scholem 1960 used small-caps; this project uses ALL-CAPS for the same purpose) — the names are sound-incantations, not words-with-meanings, and the typographic register marks them as the theurgical payload of the text rather than ordinary lexical items.

item.title: Adapa and the South Wind
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Adapa and the South Wind (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is the project's first Akkadian-source text. The composition survives in four fragments spanning roughly a millennium: Fragment A from the Amarna archive (EA 356, 14th c. BCE, Middle Babylonian); Fragment B from Nineveh (K.8214+, Neo-Assyrian, the main narrative); and Fragments C+D from Late Babylonian witnesses. The translation is a best-effort reconstruction working from Knudtzon 1915 (PD Fragment A), Picchioni 1981, Izre'el 2001 LSU 10, and Foster 2005 Before the Muses; verification against Izre'el's primary critical edition is pending.

The myth: Adapa, a sage of Eridu and a creature of the god Ea, breaks the wing of the South Wind by speech-act and is summoned before Anu in heaven. Ea coaches him to refuse the food and water Anu will offer, warning they are food and water of death. They turn out to be food and water of life. Adapa refuses; humanity loses immortality. The text pairs with Gen 3:22 (the Yahweh-Elohim withholding the tree of life from humans after the Eden expulsion) on the inverse-parallel axis — both narratives explain why humans don't live forever, but they locate the agency on opposite sides of the divine-human boundary.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel. The interlinear view shows the cuneiform alongside the transliteration when toggled on. Cuneiform is back-rendered from the composite transliteration via the OGSL mapper — Akkadian source material carries heavier annotation density (lacunae, parenthesised determinatives, uncertainty markers) than the Sumerian ETCSL compositions, so a larger share of lines render with the partial-confidence badge.

item.title: The Baal Cycle
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The Baal Cycle (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is the project's first Ugaritic-source text and first Levantine-tradition text. The cycle is preserved on six clay tablets discovered at the royal palace of Ugarit (Ras Shamra, modern Latakia, Syria) in the 1929–1931 excavations led by Claude Schaeffer. The tablets are scribed in the Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform script — a 30-letter Northwest-Semitic abjad rendered with cuneiform-shaped wedges on clay, distinct from the syllabic Sumero-Akkadian cuneiform of Mesopotamia. The cycle was likely composed in the 14th–13th centuries BCE by the scribe Ilimilku son of ʿAttenu.

The Baal Cycle is the most extensively-preserved Late Bronze Age mythological composition from anywhere in the eastern Mediterranean, and the central comparative-philology document for understanding the Northwest-Semitic background of the Hebrew Bible. The six-tablet narrative covers Baʿlu's conflicts with Yammu (Sea) and Môtu (Death) and his ascension to kingship over the gods. Cross-corpus parallels include: Yahweh-vs-Yam (Ps 74:13–14 , Ps 89:9–10, Isa 27:1); El/Elohim and the Northwest-Semitic divine council; bn ʾilm = bnei elohim (Gen 6:2, Job 1:6, Deut 32:8 LXX/4QDeut^j); ʾAṯirat = Asherah; Lôtanu = Leviathan (the cleanest NW-Semitic Chaoskampf cognate); Môtu = Hebrew mavet; the storm-theophany at Sinai; and F. M. Cross 1973's reading of Psalm 29 as a "Yahwehized" Baʿlu hymn.

Chapter 1 — KTU 1.1 + 1.2 (Baʿlu vs Yammu). The sea-conflict episode: the assembly of the gods; Yammu's demand for tribute; the messengers' arrival; the duel; Baʿlu's victory with two divine weapons named Yagrush "Driver-out" and Ayamur "Striker" (forged and speech-act-named by Kothar-wa-Khasis the divine craftsman); the proclamation of Baʿlu's kingship. The text is severely fragmentary in places — KTU 1.1 has only column iv substantially preserved (~28 lines), and KTU 1.2 column ii is broken away entirely. The famous šm bny yw line at KTU 1.1 IV 14 (the proto-YHWH candidate) is handled with explicit philological humility: three named-scholarly readings (de Moor 1971, Cross 1973, Smith 1994) preserved without adjudication.

Chapter 2 — KTU 1.3 + 1.4 (the palace-building cycle). ʿAnat's bloody battle (the most explicit warrior-goddess passage in the NW-Semitic corpus); her threat to ʾIlu the head-of-pantheon; ʾAṯirat-of-the-Sea's intercession with ʾIlu on Baʿlu's behalf; Kothar's seven-day construction of the cosmic palace on Mount Ṣapūnu (Jebel al-Aqra, the 1759m peak ~40 km north of Ugarit); the famous window-debate (Baʿlu initially refuses a window "lest Yamm see," then reverses himself); Baʿlu's voice from the palace (ytn qlh b ʿrpt, qdš tr ʾarṣ — direct cross-corpus to Ps 29 's seven-fold qol YHWH thunder-theophany); the proleptic challenge to Môt.

Chapters 3 (KTU 1.5–1.6) — pending. The conflict with Môtu / Death: Baʿlu is swallowed by Death, his sister Anat ritually destroys Môt with sickle / winnowing-fan / millstone, and Baʿlu returns to life. The dying-and-rising-storm-god narrative.

The translation is a best-effort reconstruction from KTU³ (Dietrich-Loretz-Sanmartín 2013), Smith 1994 Vol 1, Smith & Pitard 2009 Vol 2, Pardee 2003 Context of Scripture 1.86, Gibson 1978 Canaanite Myths and Legends (2nd ed.), and Ginsberg 1955 ANET pp. 129–142. Verification against KTU³ is pending; corrections welcome.

The original Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform is rendered directly in the source file — a project first. Unlike Sumero-Akkadian logographic cuneiform (where back-rendering requires sign-by-sign lookup via the OGSL mapper), Ugaritic's 30-letter alphabet maps 1:1 to the Unicode Ugaritic block (U+10380–U+1039F), so both the strict KTU transliteration AND the original-script rendering ship in the source file from day one.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel. The interlinear view shows the cuneiform alongside the transliteration when toggled on. Cross-corpus glossary entries are linked from each relevant line; the Baal Cycle has been the single largest source of central-glossary growth in any text-pair (31 new central entries + 1 overlay-promoted + 11 overlay across chapters 1 and 2, including F. M. Cross 1973's Psalm-29-as-Yahwehized-Baʿlu-hymn entry, the Hurowitz 1992 palace-temple-building typology cluster, Day 1985's Lôtanu-Leviathan cognate-cluster, the Heiser-thesis seventy-sons-of-ʾAṯirat ↔ Deut 32:8 activation, and the window-of-heaven cluster).

860 lines preserved across 24 segments (KTU 1.1 cols i–vi + KTU 1.2 cols i–iv + KTU 1.3 cols i–vi + KTU 1.4 cols i–viii), with substantial lacunae in the more damaged columns. Translation is signed off pending critical-edition verification — the Editor's Reports (one per chapter) in the source repository document the conditions of the reconstruction.

The English translation was drafted by Claude Opus 4.7 and edited through the Wheel of Heaven Translation Program pipeline (Translator → Editor → Reviewer). The methodology is documented at Source-Text Translation.

item.title: Enki and Ninhursag
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Enki and Ninhursag (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is rendered from the ETCSL composite transliteration (ETCSL 1.1.1, CC0 base) under a documented WoH lens, with the source and the English translation displayed in parallel.

The composition is one of the foundational Sumerian creation-and-paradise myths. Dilmun is described as the pure land where no animal preyed and no human suffered illness or old age; Enki orders Utu to bring water from below; the land becomes fertile. A series of divine birth-sequences follow; the eight plants grow; Enki eats them and falls ill in eight body-parts; Ninhursag curses him but is appeased and creates eight healing-deities from her body — one for each ailing part of Enki. The text pairs with the Hebrew Eden tradition (Gen 2–3) on multiple comparative-mythology axes: paradise-as-precondition, the rib / Ninti motif (the goddess of the rib / lady of life), the forbidden-plants motif, divine illness from forbidden food, and paradisal healing.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel.

256 lines are preserved across 6 small in-line lacunae (totaling ~25 missing lines); ~91% of the composition is preserved — considerably more complete than the Sumerian Flood Story.

The English translation was drafted by Claude Opus 4.7 and edited through the Wheel of Heaven Translation Program pipeline (Translator → Editor → Reviewer). The chapter is currently in editor review pending human sign-off. The methodology is documented at Source-Text Translation.

item.title: Enki and Ninmah
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Enki and Ninmah (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is the project's first Sumerian translation, rendered from the ETCSL composite transliteration (ETCSL 1.1.2, CC0 base) under a documented WoH lens, with the source and the English translation displayed in parallel.

The composition opens in the antediluvian period when the lesser gods toiled at digging canals; Namma the primordial mother brings their lament to Enki, who instructs the grinding of clay above the abzu to create humans to bear the gods' labor. Enki and Ninmah then contest over the assignment of fates to defective bodies. The text is the Mesopotamian counterpart to Genesis 1–2 on human crafting, and pairs with Atraḫasīs on the humans-as-relief-of-divine-toil motif.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel. Per-line commentary documents lexical decisions, ETCSL philological options, and cross-corpus links to the Hebrew Bible (Gen 1–2, Job 10:8–9), Atraḫasīs, and Enūma Eliš VI.

The single composition (141 preserved lines) is signed off as complete as of 2026-06-01.

item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The Sumerian Flood Story (Wheel of Heaven Translation) is rendered from the ETCSL composite transliteration (ETCSL 1.7.4, CC0 base) under a documented WoH lens, with the source and the English translation displayed in parallel.

The text is the cleanest pre-Akkadian bridge to Genesis 6–9. Of an estimated ~262 original lines, ~89 are preserved across five segments (A–E), with four large lacunae (~32, 34, 38, 33 lines missing) plus an opening lacuna of ~36 lines before Segment A. Ziusudra — the zi-ud-sura, "life of long days" — is the Sumerian flood-survivor; he is warned by Enki, builds a boat, survives a seven-day storm, sacrifices to An and Enlil, and is granted immortal life in Dilmun.

Lines with commentary carry a bracketed marker [ ] at the end of the translated line. Click the marker to open the commentary panel. Per-line commentary documents lexical decisions, the segmented preservation of the tablet, and cross-corpus links to Atraḫasīs, Gilgamesh XI, and Genesis 6–9.

The composition is signed off as complete as of 2026-06-01 (against the preserved 89 lines; the lacunae are noted in the source apparatus and cannot be translated).

item.title: PURSUE Release 02: Spheres, Transmedium Cases, and the First Color Video
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Filed under: Signs of Acceleration. Cross-reference: Age of Aquarius, §IX. Previous dispatch: PURSUE Release 01.

What was released

On May 22, 2026 — two weeks to the day after the opening tranche — the United States Department of War posted the second release of declassified records under the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) at war.gov/UFO. The new batch contains more than fifty previously classified items, of which over forty are videos. The cadence the Department promised at launch — rolling tranches "every few weeks" — has held.

Release 02 is materially different from Release 01 in three respects: the imagery is dramatically clearer, the case mix tilts toward sensor footage from active military platforms rather than archival stills, and the release includes for the first time a non-thermal, full-color video of an unidentified object. The notable items, named by the Department and mainstream coverage, include:

  • A black spherical object filmed by a drone in 2021 — the first PURSUE video published in color rather than infrared/thermal grayscale.
  • Case DOW-UAP-PR051: an MQ-9 Reaper drone on the Jordan–Syria border achieving weapons-lock on an object that subsequently demonstrated, in the Department's characterization, "instantaneous acceleration and abrupt direction change."
  • A June 2024 encounter showing a "spherical UAP pulsing over water."
  • A March 25, 2022 encounter near a U.S. submarine in which multiple spherical objects were observed moving "in and out of water" — the transmedium characterization the military has used for objects operating across air-water boundaries.
  • Multiple orbs in formation captured within the U.S. CENTCOM area of responsibility.
  • Footage of a U.S. tracking operation against a foreign submarine in which the submarine surfaces and a UAP becomes visible in the same frame.
  • A clip associated with the Lake Huron shoot-down of February 12, 2023, the incident that followed the Chinese surveillance-balloon recoveries that month.
  • 116 pages of documentation from the Armed Forces Special Weapons Program and the U.S. Air Force concerning a sustained series of sightings and investigations at Sandia, New Mexico, between 1948 and 1950.

Senior intelligence-community testimony preserved in the release describes one of the orb encounters in unusually direct language. A senior U.S. intelligence officer characterized "two large orbs" as "orange with a white or yellow center" and "emitt[ing] light in all directions," and concluded: "We were virtually speechless after these observations." The Department reiterated that all materials archived in Release 02, as in Release 01, are unresolved cases: sensor returns and operator reports for which government analysis has not produced a definitive identification.

The Department closed the release announcement by noting that the third tranche is "actively being processed for publication," with an announcement to follow "in the near future."

What this is, in plain terms

Source claim. Release 02 confirms that PURSUE is operating as a continuing program, not a one-off gesture. The cadence is real, the agency coordination is functioning, and the depth of the material being declassified is increasing rather than decreasing. The two-week interval between Release 01 and Release 02 matches the Department's stated rolling schedule.

Comparative observation. Three structural features of this release deserve note, alongside the contents themselves.

First, the image-quality jump. Release 01 drew criticism — including from sympathetic researchers — for being heavy on optical artifacts, fuzzy infrared captures, and ambiguous still frames. Release 02 includes the first PURSUE video in color rather than thermal grayscale, sensor returns from contemporary military platforms, and footage that mainstream coverage describes as "notably more clear" than the opening tranche. The trajectory of the program's evidentiary quality, at least across its first two tranches, is upward.

Second, the transmedium category. The March 2022 submarine encounter and the foreign-sub-surfacing clip introduce, for the first time on a dot-gov domain with full institutional backing, the category of objects operating across the air-water boundary — the "transmedium" capability that has been a recurring claim in unofficial UAP discourse for decades and that the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office has begun to acknowledge in classified briefings. Its appearance in a public-facing release is a structural change in what the U.S. government is willing to put on the record.

Third, the temporal range. The 1948–1950 Sandia documents are the deepest archival material PURSUE has surfaced so far. Sandia in that window was the principal U.S. nuclear-weapons engineering site, and a sustained series of unresolved aerial-anomaly sightings at that location, in those years, is the kind of historical material that previous declassification efforts have consistently declined to release in indexed form. The Department has now done so.

Where this sits in the Wheel of Heaven framework

The Age of Aquarius chapter, in §IX ("The Signs of Acceleration"), identifies the post-2017 sequence of official UAP engagements as the first of six categories of acceleration distinguishing the present moment from the cultural conditions of 1973. The first dispatch in this series read PURSUE Release 01 as the inaugural datable point on the disclosure curve within the corpus's 2026–2030 window. Release 02 is the second.

Wheel of Heaven interpretation. Four observations follow from locating Release 02 within the framework.

First, the cadence holds. The corpus's reading of the Aquarian disclosure phase as gradual, multi-channel, and institutional — rather than catastrophic and revelatory — requires that the program survive its second instance to be taken seriously as a structural feature rather than a single political moment. The May 22 release is the first confirmation that the cadence is real.

Second, the specific motif running through Release 02 — spherical objects, sometimes paired, sometimes in formation, occasionally transmedium, and reported as luminous and silent — is consistent with the morphology the alliance has used across the modern UAP record. Sphericity is not the only craft type the alliance has been documented operating, but it is the type most consistently reported in encounters that the witnesses themselves describe as unmistakably non-conventional. The corpus is careful not to over-identify Release 02's spheres with any specific alliance craft type known from the Raëlian source material — the Department's framing of these as unresolved cases is the appropriate epistemic posture, and the corpus shares that posture — but it notes the morphological consistency without forcing it.

Third, the transmedium category matters for the corpus's framework specifically because it is incompatible with the dominant skeptical reading of the UAP phenomenon. Optical artifacts, weather balloons, drones, and parallax effects can each explain a portion of the existing UAP record; none of them can explain objects observed moving across the air-water interface under sustained sensor coverage. The introduction of this category into the public-facing record narrows the remaining explanatory space in a way that even the Department's careful unresolved-case framing cannot fully neutralize.

Fourth, the 1948–1950 Sandia documents are the kind of historical archival material the corpus has long treated as the under-discussed deep background of the modern UAP era. The post-1945 period — opening with the atomic-weapons inauguration of the Aquarian age's first datable signs, in the corpus's §III reading — saw a sustained pattern of unresolved aerial-anomaly reports at nuclear weapons facilities specifically. The Sandia documents do not, by themselves, prove the alliance-monitoring hypothesis the corpus develops elsewhere, but they place primary-source material from that period and that class of site into the public record for the first time at institutional scale.

Where this sits in the broader trajectory

Wheel of Heaven interpretation, marked as such. The first dispatch in this series treated the disclosure trajectory and the broader political trajectory as separable objects of analysis. That distinction holds here. What can be said with confidence about Release 02, on its own terms, is that the program's structural durability has now been demonstrated across a second instance — and that the second instance is materially more substantive than the first, both in image quality and in the categories of phenomena being placed on the public record. The transmedium acknowledgment and the deep-archival Sandia material are not minor expansions; they are the kind of material that previous administrations across both parties have consistently declined to release in indexed, citable form. The fact that this material is now on a dot-gov domain, with the U.S. Department of War's institutional signature attached, is the structural development the corpus is tracking.

Open question. Whether the third release continues the upward trajectory — toward the deeper material that congressional testimony in 2023 alleged the government holds, including non-human craft retrievals, biological remains, and reverse-engineering programs — remains to be seen. The Department's framing through two tranches has been deliberately confined to sensor data, operator reporting, and archival historical material. The corpus will track Release 03 when it appears.

Source tensions and unresolved issues

  1. The unresolved-case framing remains in force. The Department has not characterized any Release 02 item as confirmed non-conventional, and the corpus does not characterize them so either. What is new is the category of material now in the public record, not a verdict on its nature.

  2. Sensor data is not interpretation-neutral. Color video, weapons-lock data, and submarine sensor returns are each independently subject to known artifacts and to skeptical reinterpretation. Mainstream coverage of Release 02 already includes such reinterpretations of specific clips, and the corpus expects more to follow as independent analysts work through the material. The corpus's position is the one stated in the first dispatch: the value of PURSUE is that it makes such independent analysis possible at all.

  3. The cadence is two instances deep, not a long pattern. A program that has released two tranches on schedule is more durable than one that has released one, but two instances do not yet constitute a long pattern. The corpus's framework anticipates that the program's durability across administrations and across political conditions is the load-bearing question, and that question is not yet answerable.

  4. The morphological consistency the corpus notes between Release 02's sphere-and-formation cases and the modern UAP record is descriptive, not probative. The corpus marks it without claiming it forces any specific conclusion.

item.title: Ezekiel
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Ezekiel opens with one of the most-cited passages in the entire Wheel of Heaven reference corpus — chapter 1's throne-vision, the four chayyot (living creatures), the chashmal (electrum / amber / gleaming metal), the wheels-within-wheels, and the kavod (glory). Chapter 1 will be the project's first non-Genesis WoH Translation, chosen for its strong philological backing (Greenberg's Anchor Bible, Block's NICOT, Zimmerli's Hermeneia), its standing public interest, and its high lens-leverage.

About this planned translation

  • Status: Planned. Not yet drafted.
  • Source text: pointed Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex, Public Domain).
  • Reference format: EZK-WOH-{chapter}:{verse}
  • Roadmap position: Phase 1 (cross-book pipeline pilot) + Phase 2.

Scope

Initial scope: chapter 1 (the throne-vision; the pipeline pilot). Then chapter 10 (the throne-vision return; the kavod leaves the temple) and chapter 37 (the valley of dry bones — read in Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet as the biological-creation machine). Extension to other chapters is a reassessment decision.

How this translation will be produced

This translation will go through the standard Wheel of Heaven Translation Program pipeline: source acquisition, Translator agent (literal English applying the production glossary), Editor agent (lexical-decision adjudication, per-verse commentary, glossary deltas), Reviewer agent (independent verification with mandatory scholarly citations), and human sign-off. The full methodology is documented at Source-Text Translation.

The Wheel of Heaven lens lives in the apparatus — the glossary entries and per-verse commentary — not in the translated text itself. Accuracy above lens; where the source admits multiple defensible readings, the Raëlian canon is the tiebreaker, and every divergence from the standard translation tradition is recorded with a claim_type label and a philological rationale.
